public_rationale: Anthropic’s filing documents substantial losses, but one company cannot establish that every AI company loses money. Photoroom’s reported profitability challenges the generalization, although the report lacks comparable accounts. The statement also supplies no accounting basis or thresholds for its financial descriptions. Available evidence therefore does not support a definitive score or establish that monthly subscriptions are inherently unviable.
limitations: The reporting period and company boundary require interpretation.
Reported company profitability does not by itself establish profitability of a particular subscription plan.
Financing-related accounting losses must not be treated as cash spent serving subscribers.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI services cannot make sense at a monthly rate, and every AI company loses huge sums while generating little revenue.

statement.excerpt: As a result, there really isn’t any way that these services make sense at a monthly rate, and every single AI company loses incredible amounts of money, all while failing to make that much revenue in the first place.
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

from_speaker: make sense at a monthly rate
failing to make that much revenue
our_interpretation: In context, AI companies means businesses supplying generative AI models or services, rather than every diversified company using AI.
The plain reading is that monthly subscriptions cannot sustainably cover their costs and that all companies in scope incur substantial company-wide losses.

Use calendar 2025, the latest completed annual reporting period before publication, for the unspecified ongoing financial state. Annual accounts provide a common period for company-wide profitability.
Do not assign numerical thresholds to incredible losses or little revenue.
The loss assertion cites no accounting basis. The nearby revenue examples do not supply one for losses, so the contract basis remains unknown.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable company accounts establish substantial losses throughout the stated population, and subscription economics show that monthly receipts cannot sustainably cover attributable costs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A company clearly within scope has demonstrated company-wide profitability in the target period, or a monthly subscription service has demonstrated sustainable full-cost profitability. A definitive monetary score additionally requires a stated accounting basis.

evidence.explanation: This interview-based report describes Photoroom as profitable and offering subscriptions. It is material contrary context, but provides neither an accounting basis nor a full-year profit statement; no primary financial accounts were located.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A specified accounting basis, comparable target-period company accounts and subscription cost records. A documented profitable company within the agreed scope could settle the universal loss assertion.
